mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate above 5.0% compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as liquidity tightens.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate decline below 3.0% signals robust labor market conditions that accelerate consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in >60% of instances when UNRATE is below 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) expansion signals robust consumer demand, increasing corporate earnings expectations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in >60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST rise.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS rise above 5.0% initiates active monetary tightening, reducing liquidity and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production decline below 100.0 indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate profit growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in >60% of instances when INDPRO is below 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: Payrolls growth above 156,000 thousand signals strong employment momentum, supporting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in >60% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 156,000 thousand.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) increase indicates accelerating consumer demand, boosting earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST rise.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 300.0 indicates persistent inflation, triggering central bank tightening that reduces equity market returns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 300.0.
